system.of: Taking part in patterns you cannot see whole.
system.note: A formal system in the sense of Godel, Escher, Bach. Axioms and theorems are the same kind of thing, so if the theorems are practices the axioms must be moves too. What the moves stand on is the ground: a description of the world, tested separately.

alphabet.note: The Loop Tongue. A pattern is written as a chain of arrows, closed into a loop, bracketed when it holds, and tagged with a scale.

lexicon.note: The Standing Thirds are named patterns: words, not theorems. A name lets Look recognise a pattern quickly, and a figure's two readings are what Tend and Fray do to it. Part Five now says so. Its tables and The Deck stay parked while the catalogue is reworked.

axioms.name: Look
axioms.statement: See a pattern while it runs.

sources.says: Before disturbing a system in any way, watch how it behaves and learn its history.
The observing self registers experience directly; it does not produce thoughts about it.
A behavior whose trigger you cannot name will already be running before you know it.

axioms.name: Plant
axioms.statement: Start a small act you mean to repeat.

sources.says: A new habit starts most reliably when its time and place are stated in advance.
A word is a seed and the mind is fertile ground for whatever is planted.
Change comes from deliberately building a habit: one rewarding act done until it needs no thought.

axioms.name: Tend
axioms.statement: Strengthen a loop that is running.

sources.says: Selective watering: arrange a life so the good seeds are watered several times a day.
Nothing survives without food, love included; it has to be nourished daily.
A small daily change compounds into a very large one, in either direction.

axioms.name: Fray
axioms.statement: Weaken a loop, or let it go.

sources.says: Reducing the gain of a reinforcing loop, slowing its growth, is a point of leverage.
Nothing survives without food, so what is no longer fed does not last.
A governor pairs a reinforcing loop with a balancing one that holds it back.

axiomsNote: Stated at the opening of Part Two and again in The Daily Practices: "Look, plant, tend, fray. That is the whole of it, and everything else in this part is those four moves at a larger scale or with another person in the room." Together they cover every change that can be made to a loop: read it, begin one, raise it, lower it.

rules.name: Look first
rules.statement: Moves chain, and Look comes first.

rules.name: At a scale
rules.statement: Any move can be made at self, dyad, skein or culture scale.

rules.name: With another
rules.statement: A move made with another person is made by what the two of you make together.

ground.note: What the moves stand on. These are descriptions of the world, sourced from the shelf, and each can be wrong. They are the meaning of the system, not part of its machinery.
ground.operation: A loop that holds becomes a part.
ground.operationNote: From the 2026-10-07 reconciliation (source/staging/Reconciliation.md). Something repeats; if the repetition holds it acts as one thing; that thing is a part one level up, which acts back down. The three pillars are this one operation seen three times. The same operation at every scale; the forms it makes need not repeat.

claims.name: Repetition builds
claims.statement: Small local acts, repeated with no plan of the whole, make large forms. A form lasts only while the repetition does.

statedIn.anchor: Small things, repeated without a master plan, build large things.

sources.says: A one percent daily change compounds to a very large difference over a year, in either direction.
A few simple organizing principles can produce wildly diverse self-organizing structures.
Conway's Game of Life: simple local rules per cell produce the whole pattern.
The chaos game: stepping halfway toward a random pole, repeated, draws a fractal.
A response changes the next situation, so a slight improvement feeds itself over time.

tensions.says: Reported by a shelf note, not verified at passage level: individual-level fixes draw attention away from changing the rules.

claims.name: Relation is real
claims.statement: What repeats together makes something neither part holds alone, and nothing affects without being affected.

statedIn.anchor: What repeats together becomes something new
you cannot affect without being affected

sources.says: A whole arises from relationships between lower-level things as a new independent thing; cites D. H. Lawrence on love as a third thing two people create.
A marriage has no mass or shape and is still as real as a desk or a drop of water.
A system is elements, interconnections and a purpose; it is more than the sum of its parts.
Interbeing: nothing exists separately; caring for another is caring for yourself.
The sense of a separate self depends on not noticing how much of it overlaps with other selves.

claims.name: Form becomes rule
claims.statement: A finished form is the material of the next scale, and a threshold changes what the same rule builds.

statedIn.anchor: A Global Form at one scale is a Local Rule at the next

sources.says: At each level a system shows organized state and behavior, which is the same as being a part in a larger system one level up.
Self-organizing systems generate hierarchy: subsystems aggregated into larger subsystems, cell to organ to person to group.
Hierarchies evolve from the lowest level up.
Small changes often appear to make no difference until a critical threshold is crossed.
In complex systems effects build nonlinearly; small events can produce disproportionately large changes.
Tipping is a special case of critical-mass phenomena, with different cross-over points per person.

claims.name: Chance remains
claims.statement: Repetition shifts the odds across many attempts and never removes the roll. A little chance inside a rule is what lets its form survive.
claims.note: Admitted by Sean, 2026-10-09. The manuscript already treats it as a foundation: it is the Fourth Iteration.

sources.says: An exceptional season was probably helped by luck, and luck does not repeat on demand.
People are pattern seekers who reject the idea that a regular-looking sequence came from a random process.
Managing yourself well holds no guarantee of prosperity; things regress toward the mean.
Luck matters. Habits are only the largest factor within your control.
Even pure skill has a probability of success; every action carries some risk.
Ecosystems are resilient partly through rich genetic variability, which lets them learn and evolve.

claims.name: Worth is the measure
claims.statement: A repetition is judged by whether it is worth repeating for its own sake, now.

statedIn.anchor: Would I be willing to repeat exactly this, unchanged, indefinitely?

sources.says: A values-focused life is more fulfilling than a goal-focused one because the journey itself is appreciated.
Practice so that every breath, step and action is fulfilling in itself.
There is only minimal control over the rewards for work, so the work has to be its own reason.

tensions.says: Reward is on the other side of sacrifice; response comes before reward. Pulls toward deferral.

claims.note: The Seventh Iteration already says the universe supplies no meaning and the noticing self makes it.

ground.pillarsNote: Three pillars, as the manuscript now states them. They hold up a place to stand. Leverage and Perspective are what one position on it gives: reach and view.

standpoint.name: Leverage
standpoint.statement: Some places in a nested pattern move everything built on them; most move almost nothing.
standpoint.derivation: Forms are built by repetition, what they build is real, and each becomes material for the next scale. A change near the root therefore reaches every leaf, and a change at a leaf reaches nothing above it.

statedIn.anchor: Leverage can be real and still not be yours to reach.

standpoint.note: Fractal Resistance now separates the two halves: the ladder describes the system, and which rungs you can touch depends on where you stand.

standpoint.name: Perspective
standpoint.statement: Every view is from one position inside the pattern. Depth comes only from holding more than one.
standpoint.derivation: You are a part of a larger form. A part acts only on what is near it. The form has properties no part contains. So no part holds the whole it belongs to, and that includes its view of another person, who is a whole too. What two views make together is itself a Third Thing: depth that neither view has.
standpoint.note: Named by Sean, 2026-10-09, and placed as derived from the pillars. Stated in The Three Pillars and followed to its end in The Limits of Running It Forward.

statedIn.anchor: You are a loop. You build a tree.
You are a loop. You build a tree.

sources.says: Minds deal with simplified models of reality, not reality, and mostly do not notice.
No one can read your mind, and the same limit may apply to reading your own.
Our models match the world well enough to succeed and still fall far short of representing it.
The observing self registers experience directly; the thinking self produces thoughts about it.
What is available about another person is their behavior, which can be observed more consciously.

poles.note: Ledger L1. Neither is good or bad: a pull can be a lifeline or a snare. Direction is mechanical; whether it is a lifeline or a snare is a question of worth.

candidates.name: Order costs
candidates.statement: Nothing that has stopped being paid for stays where it was left.

sources.says: No physical system grows forever in a finite environment; a balancing loop always constrains it.

candidates.note: Stated in Reading Your Own Cycle and relied on by Anchoring to What Already Turns. Folded into the first axiom for now. Shelf support is thin: one adjacent passage.

open.note: What the pillars leave open, one from each side. The world brings chance; you bring worth. Stated in The Three Pillars.

guides.name: Watch it run
guides.instruction: See the pattern while it is running, before touching it.

guides.name: Tend the act
guides.instruction: Change the small repeated thing, not the outcome.
guides.blindSpot: Blaming a person for what their conditions produce.

guides.name: Tend the between
guides.instruction: Fix how two sides translate each other, not the people.
guides.blindSpot: Repairing a relationship that should be left.

guides.name: Walk the loop
guides.instruction: Trace it round to where it started.
guides.blindSpot: Treating everything as a loop, or taking the blame for harm done to you.

guides.name: Mind what adds up
guides.instruction: Settle what can cancel; be deliberate about what only accumulates.

guides.name: Check the size
guides.instruction: A change of scale changes what the same act builds.
guides.blindSpot: Waiting on a threshold with no limit set in advance.

guides.name: Check the stand-in
guides.instruction: Ask whether the picture, the measure or the means still matches what it stands for.

guides.name: Make it worth repeating
guides.instruction: Ask whether you would repeat exactly this, unchanged, indefinitely, and whether it is yours or owed.

guides.name: Find the other pole
guides.instruction: Every running pattern can strengthen or weaken, and either can be a lifeline or a snare. Look for the reading you are not seeing.
guides.blindSpot: Looking for a second pole on something that has stopped running.

guidesNote: Advice about which move to make, and where. Not axioms, and not in the manuscript under these names. Each names its own blind spot.

derivedMoves.name: Hold
derivedMoves.statement: Tend and fray at once, so a thing stays where it is against the pull to change it.
derivedMoves.note: Not a fifth axiom, because it is made of two of the four. The ledger says the same of patterns that meet in opposite directions: they are held. Deliberately not moving is Hold, and it is work.
derivedMoves.readings: Steady or stuck. In a stable position, moving is what costs you; in a stalled one, not moving is what costs you.

statedIn.anchor: Offering it and waiting is the practice.
